## Integer type

A finite integral number inside [INTEGER_LIMITS](./contracts.integer_limits.md)<!-- -->.

**Signature:**

```typescript
type Integer = number & {
  readonly [integerBrand]: 'Integer: convert with Integer.validate(n), Integer.round(n), or Integer.truncate(n)'
}
```

## Remarks

`Integer` is assignable to `number`<!-- -->, so arithmetic and comparisons work as usual, but `number` is not assignable to `Integer`<!-- -->. To turn a `number` into an `Integer`<!-- -->, use `Integer.validate(n)` (rejects anything that is not already an integer), `Integer.round(n)` (rounds half away from zero), or `Integer.truncate(n)` (drops the fraction). Do not cast: a cast does not convert, and the value is still validated, and rejected, at runtime. An integer has no signed zero: `-0` is accepted and encodes as `0`<!-- -->.

The brand's literal repeats those helper names, so the compiler's own diagnostic for a plain `number` names the fix even without a hover.
